                "uuid": "019f9b4d-58e0-755f-8256-c6d248adbff8",
                "text": "Good question \u2014 and the answer has important legal nuance. Let me be precise here.\n\n## Short Answer\n\n**No, you cannot handle this at the Surat office.** You must visit either:\n1. **Assistant Charity Commissioner, Jamkhambhaliya** (where the original 2019 filing was made) \u2014 **primary**\n2. **Deputy Charity Commissioner, Rajkot Region** (parent regional office) \u2014 **secondary**\n3. **Charity Commissioner, Ahmedabad (Head Office)** \u2014 **last resort for state-level queries**\n\nLet me explain why the office matters legally.\n\n---\n\n## Why Jurisdiction Matters for This Query\n\nUnder the **Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950** (as applicable in Gujarat), Section 18 mandates that:\n\n> *\"Such application shall be made to the Deputy or Assistant Charity Commissioner **of the region or sub-region within the limits of which the trustee has an office for the administration of the trust or the trust property or where substantial portion of the trust property is situated.**\"*\n\n**Your trust's registered office is in Dwarka.** This falls under:\n- **Sub-region:** Devbhumi Dwarka\n- **Local Office:** Assistant Charity Commissioner, **Jamkhambhaliya**\n- **Regional Office:** Deputy Charity Commissioner, **Rajkot Region** (Jamkhambhaliya falls under Rajkot regional jurisdiction)\n- **State-level Office:** Charity Commissioner, Gujarat State, **Ahmedabad**\n\n**Surat is a completely different region.** Surat has its own Charity Commissioner office serving trusts registered in Surat and surrounding areas (South Gujarat). They:\n- Do NOT have your trust's file\n- Cannot access Jamkhambhaliya's paper records\n- Cannot verify or issue certified copies of trusts outside their jurisdiction\n- Their staff has no obligation to help with a case outside their region\n\nEven if you go to Surat, they'll politely tell you to visit Jamkhambhaliya (or route your query through Ahmedabad).\n\n---\n\n## Why This is Physical Record Territory\n\nHere's the practical reality of Indian charitable trust administration:\n\n**Paper-based system:** Each Assistant Charity Commissioner sub-office maintains its own **paper Public Trust Register (PTR)**, inward registers, order sheets, and case files. These are physical bound registers stored in the office. The Jamkhambhaliya office's PTR is in Jamkhambhaliya \u2014 not synchronized to other offices, not digitized fully, not accessible from Surat, Ahmedabad, or anywhere else.\n\n**No inter-office access:** Unlike Aadhaar or PAN which are centralized databases, Charity Commissioner records are decentralized. Each sub-office is essentially a separate records repository.\n\n**Officer authority:** The Assistant Charity Commissioner at Jamkhambhaliya is the sole authority who can:\n- Look up whether registration was completed\n- Issue certified PTR extracts\n- Confirm the registration number\n- Explain what pending action (if any) exists\n\n---\n\n## Recommended Approach \u2014 In Order\n\n### Option 1 (Best): Physical Visit to Jamkhambhaliya\n\n**Distance from Dwarka:** ~40-50 km (about 1-1.5 hours by road)\n\nThis is a day trip. Realistically, this is the fastest and most reliable route.\n\n**What to carry:**\n- Copy of Trust Deed\n- Copy of the stamped Schedule II (showing 22/07/2019 filing)\n- Copy of the affidavits\n- Copy of trust PAN card\n- Your Aadhaar\n- A signed authorization letter from your father (President) \u2014 because you're not a trustee yourself\n- \u20b9100-500 in cash for certified copy fees\n- Written application (I can help draft this)\n\n**What to ask:**\n- Confirm status of Schedule II application filed on 22/07/2019\n- Request certified copy of PTR entry (Schedule I)\n- Request certified copy of Registration Certificate\n- Ask for the exact registration number (format: G/xxx/Devbhoomi Dwarka)\n\n### Option 2 (If Physical Visit Is Difficult): RTI to Jamkhambhaliya\n\nIf you cannot travel to Jamkhambhaliya soon, file an **RTI (Right to Information)** application by post:\n\n- **Addressed to:** Public Information Officer, Office of the Assistant Charity Commissioner, Jamkhambhaliya, Dist. Devbhumi Dwarka, Gujarat\n- **Fee:** \u20b910 (via IPO \u2014 Indian Postal Order \u2014 payable to the office)\n- **Language:** Gujarati or English\n- **Response mandated within:** 30 days by law\n- **Speed:** Slower than physical visit but legally binding\n\n### Option 3 (If Both Above Fail): Escalate to Head Office\n\n**Only after** Jamkhambhaliya doesn't respond satisfactorily, then:\n- Write to **Office of the Charity Commissioner, Gujarat State, Dr. Jivraj Mehta Bhavan, Gandhinagar Highway, Ahmedabad** (verify current address \u2014 this may have changed)\n- Include copy of your Jamkhambhaliya application/RTI and their response (or non-response)\n- Ask for state-level intervention to resolve status\n\n---\n\n## Why NOT Surat Specifically\n\nI want to address this directly because I suspect you may be based in Surat, or have easier access to Surat than Dwarka right now.\n\n**Reasons Surat won't work:**\n\n1. **No file access** \u2014 Your trust's file is physically at Jamkhambhaliya. Surat's office has no reason to have it.\n\n2. **No system-level access** \u2014 Even if Surat's office wanted to help, they can't pull records from another sub-office's paper register.\n\n3. **Different jurisdiction** \u2014 Trusts registered in Surat file under Surat's Charity Commissioner. Your trust is registered in Devbhumi Dwarka jurisdiction. These are legally distinct.\n\n4. **Cannot issue certified copies** \u2014 Only the office that maintains the register can issue certified copies of entries in that register.\n\n5. **Staff will redirect you** \u2014 Best case, they'll politely tell you to visit Jamkhambhaliya.\n\n---\n\n## A Better Question You Might Be Asking\n\nIf you're asking \"can I avoid the trip to Jamkhambhaliya,\" the honest alternatives are:\n\n**Yes, you can avoid it if you:**\n\n1. **Send someone else with authority** \u2014 Your father (as President) can go directly, or authorize any advocate/CA in the Dwarka/Jamkhambhaliya area to visit on his behalf. This is often the practical solution \u2014 a local advocate in Jamkhambhaliya charging \u20b9500-2000 to handle the entire status inquiry and certified copy request.\n\n2. **File RTI by post** \u2014 Slower but doesn't require travel.\n\n3. **Engage a local advocate** \u2014 Many CA/advocate firms in Jamnagar or Jamkhambhaliya offer this as a routine service. They know the office staff, know the drill, and get results faster than an unfamiliar visitor.\n\n**No, you cannot avoid it if you try to use:**\n\n- Surat office\n- Ahmedabad head office (initially \u2014 they'll route you back)\n- Any online portal (since it doesn't show your trust)\n- Any general email inquiry\n\n---\n\n## My Practical Recommendation\n\nSince you're operating from wherever you are (Surat, based on your question), and physical Jamkhambhaliya visit may be inconvenient:\n\n**Best combined approach:**\n\n1. **Send your father to Jamkhambhaliya** \u2014 He's the President, based in Dwarka (40 km away), and can go with full legal authority. He carries all trust docs. This is ideal.\n\n2. **If your father can't go**, engage a **local advocate in Jamnagar or Dwarka** (any competent advocate practicing at Jamkhambhaliya's ACC office) to handle the entire inquiry. Cost: \u20b91,000-3,000 typically. They'll:\n - File the status inquiry\n - Get certified copies\n - Explain any pending action needed\n - Handle it all in 1-2 weeks\n\n3. **Parallel \u2014 File an RTI by post yourself** \u2014 as a backup track. Doesn't hurt to have both moving.\n\n---\n\n## Where Are You Currently Based?\n\nSince you asked about Surat specifically, I'm guessing you're operating from there. Just so I understand your logistical constraints better:\n\nAre you asking because:\n- (a) You live/work in Surat and can only visit an office there\n- (b) You'll be in Surat soon and hoped to combine trips\n- (c) You have a lawyer/CA contact in Surat you'd prefer to use\n\nLet me know and I can suggest the best route accordingly. If (c) is the answer, your Surat CA can help you draft the RTI or authorize a local advocate in Jamkhambhaliya on your behalf \u2014 that could work even if the physical visit needs to be at Jamkhambhaliya.\n\nAlso \u2014 since we're pausing operations until the CC certificate is resolved anyway, there's no rush to do this in a single day. Even 2-3 weeks to properly resolve this at the correct office is better than shortcuts that lead to dead ends.",

Some are physical actions (obtain copies, verify records).\n\n---\n\n## The List \u2014 For Your Lawyer\n\nYou can copy-paste the below directly into WhatsApp/email to your lawyer:\n\n---\n\n**\u0aa8\u0aae\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a95\u0abe\u0ab0 [\u0ab5\u0a95\u0ac0\u0ab2\u0ab6\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae],**\n\n\u0aae\u0abe\u0ab0\u0abe \u0aaa\u0ab0\u0abf\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab0\u0aa8\u0abe \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0ab8\u0a82\u0aac\u0a82\u0aa7\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0a95\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0ab2\u0ac0\u0a95 \u0aae\u0abe\u0ab9\u0abf\u0aa4\u0ac0 \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa6\u0ab8\u0acd\u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0a9c\u0acb \u0aae\u0ac7\u0ab3\u0ab5\u0ab5\u0abe \u0aae\u0abe\u0a9f\u0ac7 \u0aa4\u0aae\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac0 \u0aae\u0aa6\u0aa6 \u0a9c\u0acb\u0a88\u0a8f \u0a9b\u0ac7. \u0a95\u0ac3\u0aaa\u0abe \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa8\u0ac0\u0a9a\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aac\u0abe\u0aac\u0aa4\u0acb \u0aae\u0abe\u0a9f\u0ac7 \u0a85\u0ab8\u0abf\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0a9a\u0ac7\u0ab0\u0abf\u0a9f\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0aae\u0abf\u0ab6\u0aa8\u0ab0 \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8, \u0a9c\u0abe\u0aae\u0a96\u0a82\u0aad\u0abe\u0ab3\u0abf\u0aaf\u0abe\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aae\u0ac1\u0ab2\u0abe\u0a95\u0abe\u0aa4 \u0ab2\u0a88\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa4\u0aaa\u0abe\u0ab8 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0acb \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa6\u0ab8\u0acd\u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0a9c\u0acb \u0aae\u0ac7\u0ab3\u0ab5\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0aae\u0aa6\u0aa6 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0acb.\n\n**\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0ab5\u0abf\u0a97\u0aa4\u0acb:**\n\n- **\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae:** \u0ab8\u0acd\u0ab5. \u0aa6\u0ac7\u0ab5\u0a95\u0ac1\u0a82\u0ab5\u0ab0\u0aac\u0ac7\u0aa8 \u0a95\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0ab5\u0ab2\u0abe",

Some are physical actions (obtain copies, verify records).\n\n---\n\n## The List \u2014 For Your Lawyer\n\nYou can copy-paste the below directly into WhatsApp/email to your lawyer:\n\n---\n\n**\u0aa8\u0aae\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a95\u0abe\u0ab0 [\u0ab5\u0a95\u0ac0\u0ab2\u0ab6\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae],**\n\n\u0aae\u0abe\u0ab0\u0abe \u0aaa\u0ab0\u0abf\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab0\u0aa8\u0abe \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0ab8\u0a82\u0aac\u0a82\u0aa7\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0a95\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0ab2\u0ac0\u0a95 \u0aae\u0abe\u0ab9\u0abf\u0aa4\u0ac0 \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa6\u0ab8\u0acd\u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0a9c\u0acb \u0aae\u0ac7\u0ab3\u0ab5\u0ab5\u0abe \u0aae\u0abe\u0a9f\u0ac7 \u0aa4\u0aae\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac0 \u0aae\u0aa6\u0aa6 \u0a9c\u0acb\u0a88\u0a8f \u0a9b\u0ac7. \u0a95\u0ac3\u0aaa\u0abe \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa8\u0ac0\u0a9a\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aac\u0abe\u0aac\u0aa4\u0acb \u0aae\u0abe\u0a9f\u0ac7 \u0a85\u0ab8\u0abf\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0a9a\u0ac7\u0ab0\u0abf\u0a9f\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0aae\u0abf\u0ab6\u0aa8\u0ab0 \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8, \u0a9c\u0abe\u0aae\u0a96\u0a82\u0aad\u0abe\u0ab3\u0abf\u0aaf\u0abe\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aae\u0ac1\u0ab2\u0abe\u0a95\u0abe\u0aa4 \u0ab2\u0a88\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa4\u0aaa\u0abe\u0ab8 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0acb \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aa6\u0ab8\u0acd\u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0a9c\u0acb \u0aae\u0ac7\u0ab3\u0ab5\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0aae\u0aa6\u0aa6 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0acb.\n\n**\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0ab5\u0abf\u0a97\u0aa4\u0acb:**\n\n- **\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae:** \u0ab8\u0acd\u0ab5. \u0aa6\u0ac7\u0ab5\u0a95\u0ac1\u0a82\u0ab5\u0ab0\u0aac\u0ac7\u0aa8 \u0a95\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0ab5\u0ab2\u0abe",

It has the questions to ask the office staff/ACC and the documents to collect.\n\n---\n\n**\u0a85\u0ab8\u0abf\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0a9a\u0ac7\u0ab0\u0abf\u0a9f\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0aae\u0abf\u0ab6\u0aa8\u0ab0 \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8, \u0a9c\u0abe\u0aae\u0a96\u0a82\u0aad\u0abe\u0ab3\u0abf\u0aaf\u0abe \u0a96\u0abe\u0aa4\u0ac7 \u0aaa\u0ac2\u0a9b\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aa8\u0abe \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab6\u0acd\u0aa8\u0acb**\n\n**\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0ab5\u0abf\u0a97\u0aa4\u0acb:**\n- **\u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae:** \u0ab8\u0acd\u0ab5. \u0aa6\u0ac7\u0ab5\u0a95\u0ac1\u0a82\u0ab5\u0ab0\u0aac\u0ac7\u0aa8 \u0a95\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0ab5\u0ab2\u0abe\u0ab2 \u0aad\u0abe\u0aa3\u0a9c\u0ac0 \u0ab5\u0abf\u0aa0\u0acd\u0aa0\u0ab2\u0abe\u0aa3\u0ac0 \u0a9a\u0ac7\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0a9f\u0ac7\u0aac\u0ab2 \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\n- **\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0aa1\u0ac0\u0aa1\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0a96:** \u0ae7\u0ae8/\u0ae6\u0aec/\u0ae8\u0ae6\u0ae7\u0aef (\u0aa6\u0acd\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab0\u0a95\u0abe\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac7\u0ab2)\n- **\u0a85\u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0 (Schedule II) \u0aa6\u0abe\u0a96\u0ab2 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab2 \u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0a96:** \u0ae8\u0ae8/\u0ae6\u0aed/\u0ae8\u0ae6\u0ae7\u0aef (\u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aa8\u0abe \u0ab8\u0ac0\u0a95\u0acd\u0a95\u0abe \u0aae\u0ac1\u0a9c\u0aac)\n- **\u0ab8\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0ab2\u0ab0/\u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0ac1\u0a96:** \u0ab9\u0ab8\u0aae\u0ac1\u0a96\u0ab2\u0abe\u0ab2 \u0a95\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0ab5\u0ab2\u0abe\u0ab2 \u0ab5\u0abf\u0aa0\u0acd\u0aa0\u0ab2\u0abe\u0aa3\u0ac0\n- **\u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aa8\u0abe \u0ab8\u0ac0\u0a95\u0acd\u0a95\u0abe \u0aaa\u0ab0\u0aa8\u0abe \u0aa8\u0a82\u0aac\u0ab0\u0acb:** \u0aaa\u0ab9\u0acb\u0a82\u0a9a \u0aa8\u0a82. \u0aeb\u0aea\u0aeb, \u0a88\u0aa8\u0acd\u0ab5\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aa1 \u0aa8\u0a82. \u0aee\u0aee\u0ae6 (\u0a85\u0ab8\u0acd\u0aaa\u0ab7\u0acd\u0a9f - \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0a9a\u0a95\u0abe\u0ab8\u0ab5\u0abe)\n- **\u0aae\u0ac2\u0ab3 \u0ab5\u0a95\u0ac0\u0ab2:** \u0ab5\u0abf\u0a9c\u0aaf \u0a8f\u0aae. \u0ab5\u0abf\u0aa0\u0acd\u0aa0\u0ab2\u0abe\u0aa3\u0ac0, \u0aae\u0aa8\u0ac0\u0ab7\u0abe \u0a86\u0ab0. \u0a97\u0acb\u0aa1\u0abe\u0aa3\u0ac0 (\u0a95\u0ac3\u0ab7\u0acd\u0aa3 \u0ab6\u0acb\u0aaa\u0ac0\u0a82\u0a97 \u0ab8\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0ab0, \u0a8f\u0aae.\u0a9c\u0ac0. \u0ab0\u0acb\u0aa1, \u0aa6\u0acd\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab0\u0a95\u0abe)\n\n---\n\n**\u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0aaa\u0ac2\u0a9b\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aa8\u0abe \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab6\u0acd\u0aa8\u0acb:**\n\n**\u0ae7.** \u0aa4\u0abe. \u0ae8\u0ae8/\u0ae6\u0aed/\u0ae8\u0ae6\u0ae7\u0aef \u0aa8\u0abe \u0ab0\u0acb\u0a9c \u0aa6\u0abe\u0a96\u0ab2 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac7\u0ab2 \u0a89\u0aaa\u0ab0\u0acb\u0a95\u0acd\u0aa4 \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac0 Schedule II \u0a85\u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab9\u0abe\u0ab2\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0ab8 \u0ab6\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a9b\u0ac7?\n\n**\u0ae8.** \u0ab6\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a86 \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac0 Public Trust Register (PTR) \u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0a8f\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0a86\u0ab5\u0ac0 \u0a9b\u0ac7? \u0a9c\u0acb \u0ab9\u0abe, \u0aa4\u0acb PTR \u0aa8\u0a82\u0aac\u0ab0 \u0ab6\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a9b\u0ac7? (G/xxx/\u0aa6\u0ac7\u0ab5\u0aad\u0ac2\u0aae\u0abf \u0aa6\u0acd\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab0\u0a95\u0abe \u0a86 \u0aab\u0acb\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aae\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82)\n\n**\u0ae9.** \u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0aae\u0a82\u0a9c\u0ac2\u0ab0 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab9\u0acb\u0aaf \u0aa4\u0acb \u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0ab8\u0ab0\u0acd\u0a9f\u0abf\u0aab\u0abf\u0a95\u0ac7\u0a9f (Certificate of Registration) \u0a95\u0acd\u0aaf\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac7 \u0a88\u0ab6\u0acd\u0aaf\u0ac1 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab9\u0aa4\u0ac1\u0a82? \u0ab6\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a85\u0aae\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0a8f\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aa8\u0a95\u0ab2 \u0aae\u0ab3\u0ac0 \u0ab9\u0aa4\u0ac0? (\u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aa8\u0abe \u0aa1\u0abf\u0ab8\u0acd\u0aaa\u0ac7\u0a9a \u0ab0\u0a9c\u0abf\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0ab0\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0aa4\u0aaa\u0abe\u0ab8 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0abe\u0ab5\u0ab5\u0ac0)\n\n**\u0aea.** \u0a9c\u0acb \u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0ab9\u0a9c\u0ac1 \u0aae\u0a82\u0a9c\u0ac2\u0ab0 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0aa8\u0aa5\u0ac0, \u0aa4\u0acb \u0a95\u0aaf\u0abe \u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0ac7\u0a9c \u0aaa\u0ab0 \u0a85\u0a9f\u0a95\u0ac7\u0ab2\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a9b\u0ac7? \u0ab6\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a95\u0acb\u0a88 \u0a95\u0acd\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0ab0\u0ac0, \u0a93\u0aac\u0acd\u0a9c\u0ac7\u0a95\u0acd\u0ab6\u0aa8, \u0aaa\u0aac\u0acd\u0ab2\u0abf\u0a95\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0aab\u0ac0, \u0a95\u0ac7 \u0aa1\u0acb\u0a95\u0acd\u0aaf\u0ac1\u0aae\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0aac\u0abe\u0a95\u0ac0 \u0a9b\u0ac7?\n\n**\u0aeb.** \u0a86 \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0a97\u0ac1\u0a9c\u0ab0\u0abe\u0aa4 \u0a9a\u0ac7\u0ab0\u0abf\u0a9f\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0aae\u0abf\u0ab6\u0aa8\u0ab0\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0a93\u0aa8\u0ab2\u0abe\u0a88\u0aa8 \u0ab5\u0ac7\u0aac\u0ab8\u0abe\u0a88\u0a9f (charityonline.gujarat.gov.in) \u0aaa\u0ab0 \u0aa6\u0ac7\u0a96\u0abe\u0aa4\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0aa8\u0aa5\u0ac0. \u0ab6\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a93\u0aa8\u0ab2\u0abe\u0a88\u0aa8 \u0aa1\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0abe\u0aac\u0ac7\u0a9d\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0a8f\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac0 \u0aac\u0abe\u0a95\u0ac0 \u0a9b\u0ac7? \u0a9c\u0acb \u0ab9\u0abe, \u0aa4\u0acb \u0aa1\u0abf\u0a9c\u0abf\u0a9f\u0ab2 \u0a85\u0aaa\u0ab2\u0acb\u0aa1 \u0a95\u0acd\u0aaf\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac7 \u0aa5\u0ab6\u0ac7?\n\n**\u0aec.** \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aab\u0abe\u0a88\u0ab2 \u0aaa\u0ab0 \u0a9b\u0ac7\u0ab2\u0acd\u0ab2\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0acb\u0a88 \u0a95\u0abe\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aaf\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab9\u0ac0 (\u0a93\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aa1\u0ab0, \u0aa8\u0acb\u0a9f\u0abf\u0ab8, \u0ab9\u0ac0\u0aaf\u0ab0\u0abf\u0a82\u0a97) \u0aa5\u0a88 \u0ab9\u0acb\u0aaf \u0aa4\u0acb \u0a8f\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0a96 \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0ab5\u0abf\u0a97\u0aa4 \u0ab6\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a9b\u0ac7?\n\n**\u0aed.** \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0ac0\u0a93\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0a95\u0acb\u0a88 \u0aaa\u0aa3 \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0a95\u0abe\u0ab0\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aa8\u0acb\u0a9f\u0abf\u0ab8 \u0a95\u0ac7 \u0aaa\u0aa4\u0acd\u0ab0 \u0aae\u0acb\u0a95\u0ab2\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0a86\u0ab5\u0acd\u0aaf\u0acb \u0ab9\u0aa4\u0acb? \u0a9c\u0acb \u0ab9\u0abe, \u0aa4\u0acb \u0a95\u0a88 \u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0a96\u0ac7 \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0a95\u0aaf\u0abe \u0ab8\u0ab0\u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae\u0ac7?\n\n---\n\n**\u0aae\u0ac7\u0ab3\u0ab5\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aa8\u0abe \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0abe\u0aa3\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0aa6\u0ab8\u0acd\u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0a9c\u0acb (Certified Copies):**\n\n**\u0aee.** Schedule I (PTR entry) \u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0abe\u0aa3\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0aa8\u0a95\u0ab2\n\n**\u0aef.** \u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0ab8\u0ab0\u0acd\u0a9f\u0abf\u0aab\u0abf\u0a95\u0ac7\u0a9f (Certificate of Registration) \u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0abe\u0aa3\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0aa8\u0a95\u0ab2 - \u0a9c\u0acb \u0a88\u0ab6\u0acd\u0aaf\u0ac1 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab9\u0acb\u0aaf \u0aa4\u0acb\n\n**\u0ae7\u0ae6.** \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aab\u0abe\u0a88\u0ab2 \u0aaa\u0ab0 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac7\u0ab2 \u0a9b\u0ac7\u0ab2\u0acd\u0ab2\u0abe \u0a93\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aa1\u0ab0\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0abe\u0aa3\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0aa8\u0a95\u0ab2\n\n**\u0ae7\u0ae7.** \u0a9c\u0acb \u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0aaa\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0acd\u0aa1\u0abf\u0a82\u0a97 \u0a9b\u0ac7, \u0aa4\u0acb \u0ab9\u0abe\u0ab2\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0ab8\u0acd\u0aa5\u0abf\u0aa4\u0abf \u0aa6\u0ab0\u0acd\u0ab6\u0abe\u0ab5\u0aa4\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab2\u0ac7\u0a96\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0aa8\u0abf\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0aa6\u0aa8 (\u0ab2\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0ab0/\u0aae\u0ac7\u0aae\u0acb)\n\n---\n\n**\u0a9c\u0acb \u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0aaa\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0acd\u0aa1\u0abf\u0a82\u0a97 \u0a95\u0ac7 \u0ab2\u0ac7\u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab8 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab9\u0acb\u0aaf \u0aa4\u0acb:**\n\n**\u0ae7\u0ae8.** \u0ab9\u0ab5\u0ac7 \u0a86\u0a97\u0ab3 \u0a95\u0a88 \u0a95\u0abe\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aaf\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab9\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ab5\u0ac0 \u0aaa\u0aa1\u0ab6\u0ac7? \u0a85\u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0 \u0ab0\u0abf\u0ab5\u0abe\u0a88\u0ab5 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ac0 \u0ab6\u0a95\u0abe\u0aaf \u0a95\u0ac7 \u0aa8\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0ab8\u0ab0\u0aa5\u0ac0 \u0aab\u0abe\u0a88\u0ab2 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ab5\u0ac0 \u0aaa\u0aa1\u0ab6\u0ac7?\n\n**\u0ae7\u0ae9.** \u0a95\u0acb\u0a88 \u0aaa\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0ab2\u0acd\u0a9f\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0ac7 \u0ab2\u0ac7\u0a9f \u0aab\u0ac0 \u0ab2\u0abe\u0a97\u0ac1 \u0aaa\u0aa1\u0ab6\u0ac7?\n\n**\u0ae7\u0aea.** \u0ab0\u0abf\u0ab5\u0abe\u0a88\u0ab5\u0ab2 \u0a95\u0ac7 \u0aab\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab6 \u0aab\u0abe\u0a88\u0ab2\u0abf\u0a82\u0a97 \u0aae\u0abe\u0a9f\u0ac7 \u0a85\u0a82\u0aa6\u0abe\u0a9c\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0ab8\u0aae\u0aaf \u0a95\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0ab2\u0acb \u0ab2\u0abe\u0a97\u0ab6\u0ac7 \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0a95\u0aaf\u0abe \u0aa1\u0acb\u0a95\u0acd\u0aaf\u0ac1\u0aae\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab8 \u0a9c\u0acb\u0a88\u0ab6\u0ac7?\n\n---\n\n**\u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8 \u0ab8\u0abe\u0aa5\u0ac7 \u0aad\u0ab5\u0abf\u0ab7\u0acd\u0aaf\u0aa8\u0abe \u0ab8\u0a82\u0aaa\u0ab0\u0acd\u0a95 \u0aae\u0abe\u0a9f\u0ac7:**\n\n**\u0ae7\u0aeb.** \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0abe \u0aae\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0ab0 \u0aae\u0abe\u0a9f\u0ac7 \u0a9c\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aac\u0aa6\u0abe\u0ab0 \u0a95\u0acb\u0aa3 \u0a9b\u0ac7 (\u0ab8\u0ac7\u0a95\u0acd\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0ab0 / \u0aa1\u0ac0\u0ab2\u0abf\u0a82\u0a97 \u0a95\u0acd\u0ab2\u0abe\u0ab0\u0acd\u0a95)? \u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae, \u0ab9\u0acb\u0aa6\u0acd\u0aa6\u0acb, \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aa8\u0acb \u0aab\u0acb\u0aa8 \u0aa8\u0a82\u0aac\u0ab0/\u0a88\u0aae\u0ac7\u0ab2.\n\n**\u0ae7\u0aec.** \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab8\u0aa4\u0acd\u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab0 \u0a88\u0aae\u0ac7\u0ab2 \u0a8f\u0aa1\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab8 \u0a95\u0ac7 \u0a9c\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0abe \u0aaa\u0ab0 \u0aad\u0ab5\u0abf\u0ab7\u0acd\u0aaf\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0aaa\u0aa4\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab5\u0acd\u0aaf\u0ab5\u0ab9\u0abe\u0ab0 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ac0 \u0ab6\u0a95\u0abe\u0aaf.\n\n---\n\n**\u0a9f\u0ac0\u0aaa:**\n- \u0a86 \u0aae\u0ac1\u0ab2\u0abe\u0a95\u0abe\u0aa4 \u0ab5\u0a96\u0aa4\u0ac7 \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0aa1\u0ac0\u0aa1, Schedule II \u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0ab8\u0ac0\u0a95\u0acd\u0a95\u0abe\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab3\u0ac0 \u0aa8\u0a95\u0ab2, \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0ac0\u0a93\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0a85\u0aa7\u0abf\u0a95\u0ac3\u0aa4\u0abf \u0aaa\u0aa4\u0acd\u0ab0 (\u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0ac1\u0a96 - \u0ab9\u0ab8\u0aae\u0ac1\u0a96\u0ab2\u0abe\u0ab2 \u0ab5\u0abf\u0aa0\u0acd\u0aa0\u0ab2\u0abe\u0aa3\u0ac0 \u0aa4\u0ab0\u0aab\u0aa5\u0ac0), \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0abe PAN \u0a95\u0abe\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aa1\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aa8\u0a95\u0ab2, \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0abe\u0aa3\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0aa8\u0a95\u0ab2\u0acb\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aab\u0ac0 (\u0a85\u0a82\u0aa6\u0abe\u0a9c\u0ac7 \u20b9\u0aeb\u0ae6\u0ae6-\u0ae7\u0ae6\u0ae6\u0ae6 \u0ab0\u0acb\u0a95\u0aa1) \u0ab8\u0abe\u0aa5\u0ac7 \u0ab2\u0abe\u0ab5\u0ab5\u0ac0.\n\n---\n\n## Explanation of What Each Question Achieves\n\nLet me quickly explain the strategy behind these questions so you understand:\n\n**Questions 1-3** establish the primary fact \u2014 is the trust actually registered or not?\n\n**Questions 4-5** handle the two possible failure modes \u2014 pending status OR online-lag.\n\n**Questions 6-7** dig into whether any communication was sent (perhaps to your father) that was missed. Very common \u2014 offices send notices to old addresses that never reach.\n\n**Questions 8-11** ensure the lawyer walks out with **physical documents in hand**, not just verbal confirmations.\n\n**Questions 12-14** prepare for the worst case \u2014 if we need to file fresh, we need to know timelines and costs.\n\n**Questions 15-16** establish future communication channels so this doesn't have to be an in-person trip every time.\n\n---\n\n## Physical Documents to Send With Your Lawyer\n\nAlong with the question list, send your lawyer these documents (scans or physical copies):\n\n1. **Trust Deed** (full copy)\n2. **Stamped Schedule II** (the one dated 22/07/2019)\n3. **Affidavits** (all three trustees')\n4. **\u0ab8\u0a82\u0aae\u0aa4\u0abf \u0aaa\u0aa4\u0acd\u0ab0 (Consent Letter)**\n5. **Trust PAN card** copy\n6. **Authorization letter from your father** (as President) authorizing this lawyer to inquire and collect certified copies on behalf of the trust \u2014 this is important because the lawyer needs standing to receive certified documents\n\nIf you don't already have an authorization letter, I can draft one for you in Gujarati. Just let me know.\n\n---\n\n## Realistic Expectations\n\n**Best case outcome:** Lawyer returns with certified PTR extract showing registration number, and we can proceed to 12A/80G application within the week.\n\n**Middle case:** Registration was granted but paperwork was never sent to trustees. Lawyer collects the copies, and we're back on track.\n\n**Worst case:** Registration was never completed (paperwork got stuck). We then know exactly what needs to be done \u2014 either revive the application or file fresh.\n\n**In all three cases, we finally have clarity \u2014 which is the biggest win.**\n\nSend this list to your lawyer along with the documents, and let me know what he reports back. Once we have the answer, we can plan next steps concretely \u2014 whether that's proceeding to 12A/80G filing, reviving the application, or filing fresh.\n\nAlso \u2014 one small favor when he returns: ask him to give you a **short written summary** of what the office told him, not just verbal. Even a 3-line email/WhatsApp. Written records make future planning much easier.",

                        "text": "Ah, got it. So the list is for **what he should ask/collect at the ACC office**, not a letter to him. Let me redo this properly.\n\n---\n\n## Questions & Tasks for the ACC Office Visit\n\nSend this list to your family lawyer. It has the questions to ask the office staff/ACC and the documents to collect.\n\n---\n\n**\u0a85\u0ab8\u0abf\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0a9a\u0ac7\u0ab0\u0abf\u0a9f\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0aae\u0abf\u0ab6\u0aa8\u0ab0 \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8, \u0a9c\u0abe\u0aae\u0a96\u0a82\u0aad\u0abe\u0ab3\u0abf\u0aaf\u0abe \u0a96\u0abe\u0aa4\u0ac7 \u0aaa\u0ac2\u0a9b\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aa8\u0abe \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab6\u0acd\u0aa8\u0acb**\n\n**\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0ab5\u0abf\u0a97\u0aa4\u0acb:**\n- **\u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae:** \u0ab8\u0acd\u0ab5. \u0aa6\u0ac7\u0ab5\u0a95\u0ac1\u0a82\u0ab5\u0ab0\u0aac\u0ac7\u0aa8 \u0a95\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0ab5\u0ab2\u0abe\u0ab2 \u0aad\u0abe\u0aa3\u0a9c\u0ac0 \u0ab5\u0abf\u0aa0\u0acd\u0aa0\u0ab2\u0abe\u0aa3\u0ac0 \u0a9a\u0ac7\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0a9f\u0ac7\u0aac\u0ab2 \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\n- **\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0aa1\u0ac0\u0aa1\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0a96:** \u0ae7\u0ae8/\u0ae6\u0aec/\u0ae8\u0ae6\u0ae7\u0aef (\u0aa6\u0acd\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab0\u0a95\u0abe\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac7\u0ab2)\n- **\u0a85\u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0 (Schedule II) \u0aa6\u0abe\u0a96\u0ab2 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab2 \u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0a96:** \u0ae8\u0ae8/\u0ae6\u0aed/\u0ae8\u0ae6\u0ae7\u0aef (\u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aa8\u0abe \u0ab8\u0ac0\u0a95\u0acd\u0a95\u0abe \u0aae\u0ac1\u0a9c\u0aac)\n- **\u0ab8\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0ab2\u0ab0/\u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0ac1\u0a96:** \u0ab9\u0ab8\u0aae\u0ac1\u0a96\u0ab2\u0abe\u0ab2 \u0a95\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0ab5\u0ab2\u0abe\u0ab2 \u0ab5\u0abf\u0aa0\u0acd\u0aa0\u0ab2\u0abe\u0aa3\u0ac0\n- **\u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aa8\u0abe \u0ab8\u0ac0\u0a95\u0acd\u0a95\u0abe \u0aaa\u0ab0\u0aa8\u0abe \u0aa8\u0a82\u0aac\u0ab0\u0acb:** \u0aaa\u0ab9\u0acb\u0a82\u0a9a \u0aa8\u0a82. \u0aeb\u0aea\u0aeb, \u0a88\u0aa8\u0acd\u0ab5\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aa1 \u0aa8\u0a82. \u0aee\u0aee\u0ae6 (\u0a85\u0ab8\u0acd\u0aaa\u0ab7\u0acd\u0a9f - \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0a9a\u0a95\u0abe\u0ab8\u0ab5\u0abe)\n- **\u0aae\u0ac2\u0ab3 \u0ab5\u0a95\u0ac0\u0ab2:** \u0ab5\u0abf\u0a9c\u0aaf \u0a8f\u0aae. \u0ab5\u0abf\u0aa0\u0acd\u0aa0\u0ab2\u0abe\u0aa3\u0ac0, \u0aae\u0aa8\u0ac0\u0ab7\u0abe \u0a86\u0ab0. \u0a97\u0acb\u0aa1\u0abe\u0aa3\u0ac0 (\u0a95\u0ac3\u0ab7\u0acd\u0aa3 \u0ab6\u0acb\u0aaa\u0ac0\u0a82\u0a97 \u0ab8\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0ab0, \u0a8f\u0aae.\u0a9c\u0ac0. \u0ab0\u0acb\u0aa1, \u0aa6\u0acd\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab0\u0a95\u0abe)\n\n---\n\n**\u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0aaa\u0ac2\u0a9b\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aa8\u0abe \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab6\u0acd\u0aa8\u0acb:**\n\n**\u0ae7.** \u0aa4\u0abe. \u0ae8\u0ae8/\u0ae6\u0aed/\u0ae8\u0ae6\u0ae7\u0aef \u0aa8\u0abe \u0ab0\u0acb\u0a9c \u0aa6\u0abe\u0a96\u0ab2 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac7\u0ab2 \u0a89\u0aaa\u0ab0\u0acb\u0a95\u0acd\u0aa4 \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac0 Schedule II \u0a85\u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab9\u0abe\u0ab2\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0ab8 \u0ab6\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a9b\u0ac7?\n\n**\u0ae8.** \u0ab6\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a86 \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac0 Public Trust Register (PTR) \u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0a8f\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0a86\u0ab5\u0ac0 \u0a9b\u0ac7? \u0a9c\u0acb \u0ab9\u0abe, \u0aa4\u0acb PTR \u0aa8\u0a82\u0aac\u0ab0 \u0ab6\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a9b\u0ac7? (G/xxx/\u0aa6\u0ac7\u0ab5\u0aad\u0ac2\u0aae\u0abf \u0aa6\u0acd\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab0\u0a95\u0abe \u0a86 \u0aab\u0acb\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aae\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82)\n\n**\u0ae9.** \u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0aae\u0a82\u0a9c\u0ac2\u0ab0 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab9\u0acb\u0aaf \u0aa4\u0acb \u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0ab8\u0ab0\u0acd\u0a9f\u0abf\u0aab\u0abf\u0a95\u0ac7\u0a9f (Certificate of Registration) \u0a95\u0acd\u0aaf\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac7 \u0a88\u0ab6\u0acd\u0aaf\u0ac1 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab9\u0aa4\u0ac1\u0a82? \u0ab6\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a85\u0aae\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0a8f\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aa8\u0a95\u0ab2 \u0aae\u0ab3\u0ac0 \u0ab9\u0aa4\u0ac0? (\u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aa8\u0abe \u0aa1\u0abf\u0ab8\u0acd\u0aaa\u0ac7\u0a9a \u0ab0\u0a9c\u0abf\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0ab0\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0aa4\u0aaa\u0abe\u0ab8 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0abe\u0ab5\u0ab5\u0ac0)\n\n**\u0aea.** \u0a9c\u0acb \u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0ab9\u0a9c\u0ac1 \u0aae\u0a82\u0a9c\u0ac2\u0ab0 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0aa8\u0aa5\u0ac0, \u0aa4\u0acb \u0a95\u0aaf\u0abe \u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0ac7\u0a9c \u0aaa\u0ab0 \u0a85\u0a9f\u0a95\u0ac7\u0ab2\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a9b\u0ac7? \u0ab6\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a95\u0acb\u0a88 \u0a95\u0acd\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0ab0\u0ac0, \u0a93\u0aac\u0acd\u0a9c\u0ac7\u0a95\u0acd\u0ab6\u0aa8, \u0aaa\u0aac\u0acd\u0ab2\u0abf\u0a95\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0aab\u0ac0, \u0a95\u0ac7 \u0aa1\u0acb\u0a95\u0acd\u0aaf\u0ac1\u0aae\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0aac\u0abe\u0a95\u0ac0 \u0a9b\u0ac7?\n\n**\u0aeb.** \u0a86 \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0a97\u0ac1\u0a9c\u0ab0\u0abe\u0aa4 \u0a9a\u0ac7\u0ab0\u0abf\u0a9f\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0aae\u0abf\u0ab6\u0aa8\u0ab0\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0a93\u0aa8\u0ab2\u0abe\u0a88\u0aa8 \u0ab5\u0ac7\u0aac\u0ab8\u0abe\u0a88\u0a9f (charityonline.gujarat.gov.in) \u0aaa\u0ab0 \u0aa6\u0ac7\u0a96\u0abe\u0aa4\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0aa8\u0aa5\u0ac0. \u0ab6\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a93\u0aa8\u0ab2\u0abe\u0a88\u0aa8 \u0aa1\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0abe\u0aac\u0ac7\u0a9d\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0a8f\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac0 \u0aac\u0abe\u0a95\u0ac0 \u0a9b\u0ac7? \u0a9c\u0acb \u0ab9\u0abe, \u0aa4\u0acb \u0aa1\u0abf\u0a9c\u0abf\u0a9f\u0ab2 \u0a85\u0aaa\u0ab2\u0acb\u0aa1 \u0a95\u0acd\u0aaf\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac7 \u0aa5\u0ab6\u0ac7?\n\n**\u0aec.** \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aab\u0abe\u0a88\u0ab2 \u0aaa\u0ab0 \u0a9b\u0ac7\u0ab2\u0acd\u0ab2\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0acb\u0a88 \u0a95\u0abe\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aaf\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab9\u0ac0 (\u0a93\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aa1\u0ab0, \u0aa8\u0acb\u0a9f\u0abf\u0ab8, \u0ab9\u0ac0\u0aaf\u0ab0\u0abf\u0a82\u0a97) \u0aa5\u0a88 \u0ab9\u0acb\u0aaf \u0aa4\u0acb \u0a8f\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0a96 \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0ab5\u0abf\u0a97\u0aa4 \u0ab6\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a9b\u0ac7?\n\n**\u0aed.** \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0ac0\u0a93\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0a95\u0acb\u0a88 \u0aaa\u0aa3 \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0a95\u0abe\u0ab0\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aa8\u0acb\u0a9f\u0abf\u0ab8 \u0a95\u0ac7 \u0aaa\u0aa4\u0acd\u0ab0 \u0aae\u0acb\u0a95\u0ab2\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0a86\u0ab5\u0acd\u0aaf\u0acb \u0ab9\u0aa4\u0acb? \u0a9c\u0acb \u0ab9\u0abe, \u0aa4\u0acb \u0a95\u0a88 \u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab0\u0ac0\u0a96\u0ac7 \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0a95\u0aaf\u0abe \u0ab8\u0ab0\u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae\u0ac7?\n\n---\n\n**\u0aae\u0ac7\u0ab3\u0ab5\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aa8\u0abe \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0abe\u0aa3\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0aa6\u0ab8\u0acd\u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0a9c\u0acb (Certified Copies):**\n\n**\u0aee.** Schedule I (PTR entry) \u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0abe\u0aa3\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0aa8\u0a95\u0ab2\n\n**\u0aef.** \u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0ab8\u0ab0\u0acd\u0a9f\u0abf\u0aab\u0abf\u0a95\u0ac7\u0a9f (Certificate of Registration) \u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0abe\u0aa3\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0aa8\u0a95\u0ab2 - \u0a9c\u0acb \u0a88\u0ab6\u0acd\u0aaf\u0ac1 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab9\u0acb\u0aaf \u0aa4\u0acb\n\n**\u0ae7\u0ae6.** \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aab\u0abe\u0a88\u0ab2 \u0aaa\u0ab0 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac7\u0ab2 \u0a9b\u0ac7\u0ab2\u0acd\u0ab2\u0abe \u0a93\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aa1\u0ab0\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0abe\u0aa3\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0aa8\u0a95\u0ab2\n\n**\u0ae7\u0ae7.** \u0a9c\u0acb \u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0aaa\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0acd\u0aa1\u0abf\u0a82\u0a97 \u0a9b\u0ac7, \u0aa4\u0acb \u0ab9\u0abe\u0ab2\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0ab8\u0acd\u0aa5\u0abf\u0aa4\u0abf \u0aa6\u0ab0\u0acd\u0ab6\u0abe\u0ab5\u0aa4\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab2\u0ac7\u0a96\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0aa8\u0abf\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0aa6\u0aa8 (\u0ab2\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0ab0/\u0aae\u0ac7\u0aae\u0acb)\n\n---\n\n**\u0a9c\u0acb \u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0aaa\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0acd\u0aa1\u0abf\u0a82\u0a97 \u0a95\u0ac7 \u0ab2\u0ac7\u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab8 \u0aa5\u0aaf\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab9\u0acb\u0aaf \u0aa4\u0acb:**\n\n**\u0ae7\u0ae8.** \u0ab9\u0ab5\u0ac7 \u0a86\u0a97\u0ab3 \u0a95\u0a88 \u0a95\u0abe\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aaf\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab9\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ab5\u0ac0 \u0aaa\u0aa1\u0ab6\u0ac7? \u0a85\u0ab0\u0a9c\u0ac0 \u0ab0\u0abf\u0ab5\u0abe\u0a88\u0ab5 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ac0 \u0ab6\u0a95\u0abe\u0aaf \u0a95\u0ac7 \u0aa8\u0ab5\u0ac7\u0ab8\u0ab0\u0aa5\u0ac0 \u0aab\u0abe\u0a88\u0ab2 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ab5\u0ac0 \u0aaa\u0aa1\u0ab6\u0ac7?\n\n**\u0ae7\u0ae9.** \u0a95\u0acb\u0a88 \u0aaa\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0ab2\u0acd\u0a9f\u0ac0 \u0a95\u0ac7 \u0ab2\u0ac7\u0a9f \u0aab\u0ac0 \u0ab2\u0abe\u0a97\u0ac1 \u0aaa\u0aa1\u0ab6\u0ac7?\n\n**\u0ae7\u0aea.** \u0ab0\u0abf\u0ab5\u0abe\u0a88\u0ab5\u0ab2 \u0a95\u0ac7 \u0aab\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab6 \u0aab\u0abe\u0a88\u0ab2\u0abf\u0a82\u0a97 \u0aae\u0abe\u0a9f\u0ac7 \u0a85\u0a82\u0aa6\u0abe\u0a9c\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0ab8\u0aae\u0aaf \u0a95\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0ab2\u0acb \u0ab2\u0abe\u0a97\u0ab6\u0ac7 \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0a95\u0aaf\u0abe \u0aa1\u0acb\u0a95\u0acd\u0aaf\u0ac1\u0aae\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab8 \u0a9c\u0acb\u0a88\u0ab6\u0ac7?\n\n---\n\n**\u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8 \u0ab8\u0abe\u0aa5\u0ac7 \u0aad\u0ab5\u0abf\u0ab7\u0acd\u0aaf\u0aa8\u0abe \u0ab8\u0a82\u0aaa\u0ab0\u0acd\u0a95 \u0aae\u0abe\u0a9f\u0ac7:**\n\n**\u0ae7\u0aeb.** \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0abe \u0aae\u0ac7\u0a9f\u0ab0 \u0aae\u0abe\u0a9f\u0ac7 \u0a9c\u0ab5\u0abe\u0aac\u0aa6\u0abe\u0ab0 \u0a95\u0acb\u0aa3 \u0a9b\u0ac7 (\u0ab8\u0ac7\u0a95\u0acd\u0ab6\u0aa8 \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0ab0 / \u0aa1\u0ac0\u0ab2\u0abf\u0a82\u0a97 \u0a95\u0acd\u0ab2\u0abe\u0ab0\u0acd\u0a95)? \u0aa8\u0abe\u0aae, \u0ab9\u0acb\u0aa6\u0acd\u0aa6\u0acb, \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aa8\u0acb \u0aab\u0acb\u0aa8 \u0aa8\u0a82\u0aac\u0ab0/\u0a88\u0aae\u0ac7\u0ab2.\n\n**\u0ae7\u0aec.** \u0a93\u0aab\u0abf\u0ab8\u0aa8\u0ac1\u0a82 \u0ab8\u0aa4\u0acd\u0aa4\u0abe\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab0 \u0a88\u0aae\u0ac7\u0ab2 \u0a8f\u0aa1\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ac7\u0ab8 \u0a95\u0ac7 \u0a9c\u0ac7\u0aa8\u0abe \u0aaa\u0ab0 \u0aad\u0ab5\u0abf\u0ab7\u0acd\u0aaf\u0aae\u0abe\u0a82 \u0aaa\u0aa4\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab5\u0acd\u0aaf\u0ab5\u0ab9\u0abe\u0ab0 \u0a95\u0ab0\u0ac0 \u0ab6\u0a95\u0abe\u0aaf.\n\n---\n\n**\u0a9f\u0ac0\u0aaa:**\n- \u0a86 \u0aae\u0ac1\u0ab2\u0abe\u0a95\u0abe\u0aa4 \u0ab5\u0a96\u0aa4\u0ac7 \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f \u0aa1\u0ac0\u0aa1, Schedule II \u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0ab8\u0ac0\u0a95\u0acd\u0a95\u0abe\u0ab5\u0abe\u0ab3\u0ac0 \u0aa8\u0a95\u0ab2, \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0ac0\u0a93\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0a85\u0aa7\u0abf\u0a95\u0ac3\u0aa4\u0abf \u0aaa\u0aa4\u0acd\u0ab0 (\u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0ac1\u0a96 - \u0ab9\u0ab8\u0aae\u0ac1\u0a96\u0ab2\u0abe\u0ab2 \u0ab5\u0abf\u0aa0\u0acd\u0aa0\u0ab2\u0abe\u0aa3\u0ac0 \u0aa4\u0ab0\u0aab\u0aa5\u0ac0), \u0a9f\u0acd\u0ab0\u0ab8\u0acd\u0a9f\u0aa8\u0abe PAN \u0a95\u0abe\u0ab0\u0acd\u0aa1\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aa8\u0a95\u0ab2, \u0a85\u0aa8\u0ac7 \u0aaa\u0acd\u0ab0\u0aae\u0abe\u0aa3\u0abf\u0aa4 \u0aa8\u0a95\u0ab2\u0acb\u0aa8\u0ac0 \u0aab\u0ac0 (\u0a85\u0a82\u0aa6\u0abe\u0a9c\u0ac7 \u20b9\u0aeb\u0ae6\u0ae6-\u0ae7\u0ae6\u0ae6\u0ae6 \u0ab0\u0acb\u0a95\u0aa1) \u0ab8\u0abe\u0aa5\u0ac7 \u0ab2\u0abe\u0ab5\u0ab5\u0ac0.\n\n---\n\n## Explanation of What Each Question Achieves\n\nLet me quickly explain the strategy behind these questions so you understand:\n\n**Questions 1-3** establish the primary fact \u2014 is the trust actually registered or not?\n\n**Questions 4-5** handle the two possible failure modes \u2014 pending status OR online-lag.\n\n**Questions 6-7** dig into whether any communication was sent (perhaps to your father) that was missed. Very common \u2014 offices send notices to old addresses that never reach.\n\n**Questions 8-11** ensure the lawyer walks out with **physical documents in hand**, not just verbal confirmations.\n\n**Questions 12-14** prepare for the worst case \u2014 if we need to file fresh, we need to know timelines and costs.\n\n**Questions 15-16** establish future communication channels so this doesn't have to be an in-person trip every time.\n\n---\n\n## Physical Documents to Send With Your Lawyer\n\nAlong with the question list, send your lawyer these documents (scans or physical copies):\n\n1. **Trust Deed** (full copy)\n2. **Stamped Schedule II** (the one dated 22/07/2019)\n3. **Affidavits** (all three trustees')\n4. **\u0ab8\u0a82\u0aae\u0aa4\u0abf \u0aaa\u0aa4\u0acd\u0ab0 (Consent Letter)**\n5. **Trust PAN card** copy\n6. **Authorization letter from your father** (as President) authorizing this lawyer to inquire and collect certified copies on behalf of the trust \u2014 this is important because the lawyer needs standing to receive certified documents\n\nIf you don't already have an authorization letter, I can draft one for you in Gujarati. Just let me know.\n\n---\n\n## Realistic Expectations\n\n**Best case outcome:** Lawyer returns with certified PTR extract showing registration number, and we can proceed to 12A/80G application within the week.\n\n**Middle case:** Registration was granted but paperwork was never sent to trustees. Lawyer collects the copies, and we're back on track.\n\n**Worst case:** Registration was never completed (paperwork got stuck). We then know exactly what needs to be done \u2014 either revive the application or file fresh.\n\n**In all three cases, we finally have clarity \u2014 which is the biggest win.**\n\nSend this list to your lawyer along with the documents, and let me know what he reports back. Once we have the answer, we can plan next steps concretely \u2014 whether that's proceeding to 12A/80G filing, reviving the application, or filing fresh.\n\nAlso \u2014 one small favor when he returns: ask him to give you a **short written summary** of what the office told him, not just verbal. Even a 3-line email/WhatsApp. Written records make future planning much easier.",

                "uuid": "019f9b56-26b5-746d-af92-234596a1270a",
                "text": "Good pause \u2014 let's use this time productively to plan the 12A/12AB and 80G roadmap. When the CC certificate arrives, you'll want to file within days, not weeks. So knowing eligibility inside-out now saves time later.\n\nLet me lay this out based on the current Income Tax framework (post-2020 amendments under Section 12AB).\n\n## First \u2014 A Quick Framing\n\n**12A (now 12AB)** and **80G** are two separate registrations, but they're filed together on the same form (Form 10A) and reviewed together. So eligibility for both largely overlaps, with a few extra conditions for 80G.\n\n**Current regime:** All new trusts get **Provisional Registration first** (valid 3 years), then convert to **Regular Registration** (valid 5 years, renewable).\n\n---\n\n## Eligibility for 12AB (Provisional Registration)\n\n### A. Type of Entity\n\nThe trust must be one of:\n- **Public Charitable Trust** \u2713 (your case)\n- Public Religious Trust\n- Society registered under Societies Registration Act\n- Section 8 Company (companies for charitable purpose)\n\n**Private trusts (family trusts, HUF trusts) are NOT eligible.** Your trust is public charitable \u2014 you qualify.\n\n### B. Charitable Purpose (Section 2(15) of Income Tax Act)\n\nThe trust's objectives must fall within the definition of \"charitable purpose\":\n\n1. **Relief of the poor**\n2. **Education**\n3. **Yoga**\n4. **Medical relief**\n5. **Preservation of environment** (including watersheds, forests, wildlife)\n6. **Preservation of monuments/places of artistic or historic interest**\n7. **Advancement of any other object of general public utility**\n\n**Your trust's Schedule III lists 25 objectives** covering healthcare, education, water resources, animal welfare, women/youth support, environmental awareness, etc. \u2014 all of these fall squarely within Section 2(15). \u2713 You qualify.\n\n### C. Non-Profit Nature\n\n- Trust income must not be distributed to trustees or their relatives\n- No trustee should benefit personally from trust funds (except reasonable remuneration for services rendered)\n- Surplus must be applied for charitable purposes\n\nYour trust deed explicitly states this. \u2713 You qualify.\n\n### D. Foundational Documents\n\nYou must have:\n- **Trust Deed** \u2713 (you have)\n- **PAN of the Trust** \u2713 (AAZTS5070P)\n- **Registration under Charity Commissioner** \u26a0\ufe0f (this is what we're trying to verify)\n- **Bank account of the trust** \u2713\n- **NGO Darpan Unique ID** \u2713\n\nThe one missing piece \u2014 CC registration certificate \u2014 is the blocker. Once obtained, all conditions are met.\n\n### E. Timing Rule\n\nUnder the new regime, **fresh applications must be filed as follows:**\n\n- **For newly established trusts (not yet started activity):** Apply for **Provisional Registration** using Form 10A. Given your trust was registered in 2019 but hasn't operationalized, you fall in this category.\n\n- **For trusts that have started activity:** Directly apply for **Regular Registration** using Form 10AB.\n\nYour trust has effectively not operated. So you file Form 10A for **Provisional Registration first**.\n\n### F. Ineligibility Triggers (Things That Disqualify)\n\nYou will be disqualified if:\n\n1. **Trust benefits only a particular religious community or caste** \u2014 Your deed explicitly states the trust serves all irrespective of caste, religion, gender, language. \u2713 Safe.\n\n2. **Objects include activities for private benefit of settler/trustees or their relatives** \u2014 Not in your deed. \u2713 Safe.\n\n3. **Trust engages in commercial activity beyond 20% of receipts** (proviso to Section 2(15) \u2014 for trusts in \"advancement of any other object of general public utility\" category) \u2014 Not an issue for you initially since there's no commercial activity.\n\n4. **Any of the trustees has been convicted of an offence** \u2014 Assumed not applicable.\n\n5. **Trust's income has been applied for benefit of specified persons under Section 13(3)** \u2014 Not applicable at start.\n\n6. **False or incomplete information in the application** \u2014 Ensure honesty when filing.\n\n---\n\n## Additional Eligibility for 80G (On Top of 12AB)\n\n80G has all the above conditions PLUS these extra ones:\n\n### G. Universal Benefit\n\nThe trust must **not exist for the benefit of any particular religious community or caste** \u2014 you're safe here, deed is explicit about universal service.\n\n### H. Books of Accounts\n\nThe trust must **maintain regular books of accounts** \u2014 you'll need to start this from Day 1 of operations. Any competent CA can set up basic accounting.\n\n### I. Non-Political\n\nThe trust must **not engage in political activities or influence elections** \u2014 your deed says non-political. \u2713 Safe.\n\n### J. 85% Application of Income\n\nThe trust must apply **at least 85% of its income towards charitable purposes** in the same financial year. Failure means 12A/80G exemption doesn't kick in for that year.\n\n### K. Corpus Rules\n\nAny corpus donations (donations to build permanent fund) must be shown separately and are exempt from the 85% rule. Regular donations are subject to 85% rule.\n\n---\n\n## Documents Required for Form 10A Filing\n\nWhen we get to actual filing, here's the checklist:\n\n**Mandatory:**\n1. Self-certified copy of **Trust Deed** (with all amendments if any)\n2. Self-certified copy of **Charity Commissioner Registration Certificate** \u26a0\ufe0f\n3. Self-certified copy of **PAN of trust**\n4. Self-certified copies of **Aadhaar of all trustees**\n5. Self-certified copies of **PAN of all trustees**\n6. **Bank account details** of the trust\n7. **NGO Darpan Unique ID** \u2713 (you have)\n8. **Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)** of the authorized signatory (Vishwa) \u2014 OR Aadhaar OTP-based e-verification\n9. **List of activities** \u2014 current and proposed (a narrative document)\n10. **Financial statements** \u2014 for past 3 years IF activities have occurred (in your case, none \u2014 you'll declare nil)\n\n**For 80G additionally:**\n11. **List of names, addresses, PAN of donors** (if any past donations received \u2014 for you, none)\n12. **Details of major activities**\n\n---\n\n## The Bigger Picture \u2014 What You Really Need to Know\n\n### Timeline Once You Have the CC Certificate\n\n| Step | Time |\n|---|---|\n| Prepare and file Form 10A on IT portal | 1-2 days |\n| CBDT processes application | 15-30 days |\n| Provisional 12AB order (Form 10AC) issued | ~30 days total |\n| Provisional 80G order issued | Same time (filed together) |\n\n**So realistically:** 30-45 days from CC certificate to having full 12A + 80G in hand.\n\n### Validity Periods\n\n- **Provisional 12AB:** Valid for **3 years**\n- **Provisional 80G:** Valid for **3 years**\n\nWithin these 3 years, once you've started meaningful activities, you must apply for **Regular Registration** using **Form 10AB**. That converts provisional to regular for **5 years**, renewable perpetually.\n\n### Cost\n\n- **Government fee for Form 10A:** \u20b90 (zero \u2014 no government fee)\n- **CA/lawyer fee (if you use one):** \u20b95,000-\u20b915,000 typically for pan-India CAs\n- **DSC cost (if using DSC):** \u20b91,500-\u20b92,500 (one-time)\n- **DIY option:** Free, using Aadhaar OTP-based e-verification\n\n### Post-Registration Compliance\n\nOnce registered, you must:\n\n1. **Maintain proper books of accounts** \u2014 mandatory audit if income exceeds \u20b92.5 lakhs (basic exemption limit)\n2. **Get accounts audited by a CA** if income exceeds threshold \u2014 filed as **Form 10B/10BB**\n3. **File ITR-7** annually by 31st October (with audit) or 31st July (without audit) \u2014 filing an ITR is mandatory even for zero income once registered\n4. **Apply 85% of income** to charitable purposes in the same year\n5. **File Form 10BD** (statement of donations received) by 31st May annually \u2014 mandatory for 80G-registered trusts\n6. **Issue Form 10BE certificates** to donors (donation receipts) so they can claim 80G deduction\n7. **Change reports to CC** for any change in trustees, address, or object (Section 22 BPT Act)\n8. **Change reports to IT Department** for changes affecting registration\n\n---\n\n## Special Consideration for Your Trust\n\nThere's one nuance worth flagging.\n\n**Your trust was created in 2019 but hasn't operated.** When filing Form 10A, in the \"activities\" section, you'll declare:\n- \"Trust has not commenced operations since incorporation. Commencement expected [date].\"\n- Attach the future activity plan\n\nThis is 100% acceptable. The IT Department grants Provisional Registration precisely for trusts in this stage \u2014 the whole point of \"provisional\" is to let trusts get tax status BEFORE they start operations, so they can operate compliantly from Day 1.\n\n**Do not worry about the 7-year gap** between trust deed (2019) and now (2026). It's not a legal problem for 12A/80G application \u2014 you just note that the trust was dormant.\n\n---\n\n## What You Can Do Right Now (Today/Sunday)\n\nSince you can't do anything on the CC side today, but want to be productive, here are things you CAN prepare in advance:\n\n### 1. Draft the \"Activities Note\"\n\nWrite a 1-2 page document titled **\"Trust Activities \u2014 Current Status and Future Plans\"**:\n- Brief history of trust (registered 2019, dormant, being activated 2026)\n- Current activities (none, or specifically list what you plan to start with)\n- Future activities planned for next 3 years (be specific \u2014 e.g., \"medical camps in Dwarka area,\" \"scholarship program for underprivileged students,\" \"old-age home support\")\n- Approximate budget estimates\n\nThis document will be uploaded with Form 10A. Having it ready now saves time.\n\n### 2. Prepare Trustees' Documents Bundle\n\nCreate a single PDF containing:\n- All 3 trustees' PAN cards (self-attested)\n- All 3 trustees' Aadhaar cards (self-attested)\n- Trust PAN card\n- Trust Deed\n\nThis is what you'll upload with Form 10A. Save time later.\n\n### 3. Decide on E-verification Method\n\nChoose one:\n- **Aadhaar OTP-based** \u2014 free, but requires Vishwa's Aadhaar-linked mobile to be active during filing\n- **Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)** \u2014 \u20b91,500-\u20b92,500 one-time cost, but easier for repeated filings\n\nFor a small trust just starting, Aadhaar OTP is fine. DSC becomes useful once operations scale.\n\n### 4. Plan the Bank Account Setup\n\nVerify with the bank:\n- Is the trust account a **current account or savings account**? (For trusts, current account is preferred)\n- Is **online banking activated** for the trust account? You'll need this for future compliance.\n- Is the **address on bank records** consistent with what we've entered on IT portal? Mismatch causes future headaches.\n\n### 5. Familiarize Yourself with Form 10A\n\nLog in (only for viewing, not filing) to the trust's IT portal account. Navigate:\n- **e-File** \u2192 **Income Tax Forms** \u2192 **File Income Tax Forms** \u2192 search for **Form 10A**\n\nJust view the form structure. Don't fill anything. Understanding the form fields in advance saves time when we file for real.\n\n---\n\n## To Answer Your Direct Question \u2014 Are You Eligible?\n\n**Yes, unequivocally.** Your trust meets all eligibility criteria for both **Provisional 12AB** and **Provisional 80G** registration.\n\nThe only pending piece is documentary proof of Charity Commissioner registration \u2014 which your lawyer will resolve when he visits Jamkhambhaliya after Monday. Once that document is in hand, we can file Form 10A within 24-48 hours.\n\nEverything else \u2014 trust structure, objectives, trustees, non-profit nature, universal benefit, non-political stance \u2014 is in perfect alignment with the requirements.\n\n---\n\nWant me to help you draft the **Activities Note** for Form 10A right now? That's the most valuable deliverable you can prepare while waiting for the CC status. If you tell me what activities you plan to start with (or want to start with) once operations begin, I can draft a solid 1-2 page document that will hold up perfectly for the 12A/80G application.",

                        "text": "Good pause \u2014 let's use this time productively to plan the 12A/12AB and 80G roadmap. When the CC certificate arrives, you'll want to file within days, not weeks. So knowing eligibility inside-out now saves time later.\n\nLet me lay this out based on the current Income Tax framework (post-2020 amendments under Section 12AB).\n\n## First \u2014 A Quick Framing\n\n**12A (now 12AB)** and **80G** are two separate registrations, but they're filed together on the same form (Form 10A) and reviewed together. So eligibility for both largely overlaps, with a few extra conditions for 80G.\n\n**Current regime:** All new trusts get **Provisional Registration first** (valid 3 years), then convert to **Regular Registration** (valid 5 years, renewable).\n\n---\n\n## Eligibility for 12AB (Provisional Registration)\n\n### A. Type of Entity\n\nThe trust must be one of:\n- **Public Charitable Trust** \u2713 (your case)\n- Public Religious Trust\n- Society registered under Societies Registration Act\n- Section 8 Company (companies for charitable purpose)\n\n**Private trusts (family trusts, HUF trusts) are NOT eligible.** Your trust is public charitable \u2014 you qualify.\n\n### B. Charitable Purpose (Section 2(15) of Income Tax Act)\n\nThe trust's objectives must fall within the definition of \"charitable purpose\":\n\n1. **Relief of the poor**\n2. **Education**\n3. **Yoga**\n4. **Medical relief**\n5. **Preservation of environment** (including watersheds, forests, wildlife)\n6. **Preservation of monuments/places of artistic or historic interest**\n7. **Advancement of any other object of general public utility**\n\n**Your trust's Schedule III lists 25 objectives** covering healthcare, education, water resources, animal welfare, women/youth support, environmental awareness, etc. \u2014 all of these fall squarely within Section 2(15). \u2713 You qualify.\n\n### C. Non-Profit Nature\n\n- Trust income must not be distributed to trustees or their relatives\n- No trustee should benefit personally from trust funds (except reasonable remuneration for services rendered)\n- Surplus must be applied for charitable purposes\n\nYour trust deed explicitly states this. \u2713 You qualify.\n\n### D. Foundational Documents\n\nYou must have:\n- **Trust Deed** \u2713 (you have)\n- **PAN of the Trust** \u2713 (AAZTS5070P)\n- **Registration under Charity Commissioner** \u26a0\ufe0f (this is what we're trying to verify)\n- **Bank account of the trust** \u2713\n- **NGO Darpan Unique ID** \u2713\n\nThe one missing piece \u2014 CC registration certificate \u2014 is the blocker. Once obtained, all conditions are met.\n\n### E. Timing Rule\n\nUnder the new regime, **fresh applications must be filed as follows:**\n\n- **For newly established trusts (not yet started activity):** Apply for **Provisional Registration** using Form 10A. Given your trust was registered in 2019 but hasn't operationalized, you fall in this category.\n\n- **For trusts that have started activity:** Directly apply for **Regular Registration** using Form 10AB.\n\nYour trust has effectively not operated. So you file Form 10A for **Provisional Registration first**.\n\n### F. Ineligibility Triggers (Things That Disqualify)\n\nYou will be disqualified if:\n\n1. **Trust benefits only a particular religious community or caste** \u2014 Your deed explicitly states the trust serves all irrespective of caste, religion, gender, language. \u2713 Safe.\n\n2. **Objects include activities for private benefit of settler/trustees or their relatives** \u2014 Not in your deed. \u2713 Safe.\n\n3. **Trust engages in commercial activity beyond 20% of receipts** (proviso to Section 2(15) \u2014 for trusts in \"advancement of any other object of general public utility\" category) \u2014 Not an issue for you initially since there's no commercial activity.\n\n4. **Any of the trustees has been convicted of an offence** \u2014 Assumed not applicable.\n\n5. **Trust's income has been applied for benefit of specified persons under Section 13(3)** \u2014 Not applicable at start.\n\n6. **False or incomplete information in the application** \u2014 Ensure honesty when filing.\n\n---\n\n## Additional Eligibility for 80G (On Top of 12AB)\n\n80G has all the above conditions PLUS these extra ones:\n\n### G. Universal Benefit\n\nThe trust must **not exist for the benefit of any particular religious community or caste** \u2014 you're safe here, deed is explicit about universal service.\n\n### H. Books of Accounts\n\nThe trust must **maintain regular books of accounts** \u2014 you'll need to start this from Day 1 of operations. Any competent CA can set up basic accounting.\n\n### I. Non-Political\n\nThe trust must **not engage in political activities or influence elections** \u2014 your deed says non-political. \u2713 Safe.\n\n### J. 85% Application of Income\n\nThe trust must apply **at least 85% of its income towards charitable purposes** in the same financial year. Failure means 12A/80G exemption doesn't kick in for that year.\n\n### K. Corpus Rules\n\nAny corpus donations (donations to build permanent fund) must be shown separately and are exempt from the 85% rule. Regular donations are subject to 85% rule.\n\n---\n\n## Documents Required for Form 10A Filing\n\nWhen we get to actual filing, here's the checklist:\n\n**Mandatory:**\n1. Self-certified copy of **Trust Deed** (with all amendments if any)\n2. Self-certified copy of **Charity Commissioner Registration Certificate** \u26a0\ufe0f\n3. Self-certified copy of **PAN of trust**\n4. Self-certified copies of **Aadhaar of all trustees**\n5. Self-certified copies of **PAN of all trustees**\n6. **Bank account details** of the trust\n7. **NGO Darpan Unique ID** \u2713 (you have)\n8. **Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)** of the authorized signatory (Vishwa) \u2014 OR Aadhaar OTP-based e-verification\n9. **List of activities** \u2014 current and proposed (a narrative document)\n10. **Financial statements** \u2014 for past 3 years IF activities have occurred (in your case, none \u2014 you'll declare nil)\n\n**For 80G additionally:**\n11. **List of names, addresses, PAN of donors** (if any past donations received \u2014 for you, none)\n12. **Details of major activities**\n\n---\n\n## The Bigger Picture \u2014 What You Really Need to Know\n\n### Timeline Once You Have the CC Certificate\n\n| Step | Time |\n|---|---|\n| Prepare and file Form 10A on IT portal | 1-2 days |\n| CBDT processes application | 15-30 days |\n| Provisional 12AB order (Form 10AC) issued | ~30 days total |\n| Provisional 80G order issued | Same time (filed together) |\n\n**So realistically:** 30-45 days from CC certificate to having full 12A + 80G in hand.\n\n### Validity Periods\n\n- **Provisional 12AB:** Valid for **3 years**\n- **Provisional 80G:** Valid for **3 years**\n\nWithin these 3 years, once you've started meaningful activities, you must apply for **Regular Registration** using **Form 10AB**. That converts provisional to regular for **5 years**, renewable perpetually.\n\n### Cost\n\n- **Government fee for Form 10A:** \u20b90 (zero \u2014 no government fee)\n- **CA/lawyer fee (if you use one):** \u20b95,000-\u20b915,000 typically for pan-India CAs\n- **DSC cost (if using DSC):** \u20b91,500-\u20b92,500 (one-time)\n- **DIY option:** Free, using Aadhaar OTP-based e-verification\n\n### Post-Registration Compliance\n\nOnce registered, you must:\n\n1. **Maintain proper books of accounts** \u2014 mandatory audit if income exceeds \u20b92.5 lakhs (basic exemption limit)\n2. **Get accounts audited by a CA** if income exceeds threshold \u2014 filed as **Form 10B/10BB**\n3. **File ITR-7** annually by 31st October (with audit) or 31st July (without audit) \u2014 filing an ITR is mandatory even for zero income once registered\n4. **Apply 85% of income** to charitable purposes in the same year\n5. **File Form 10BD** (statement of donations received) by 31st May annually \u2014 mandatory for 80G-registered trusts\n6. **Issue Form 10BE certificates** to donors (donation receipts) so they can claim 80G deduction\n7. **Change reports to CC** for any change in trustees, address, or object (Section 22 BPT Act)\n8. **Change reports to IT Department** for changes affecting registration\n\n---\n\n## Special Consideration for Your Trust\n\nThere's one nuance worth flagging.\n\n**Your trust was created in 2019 but hasn't operated.** When filing Form 10A, in the \"activities\" section, you'll declare:\n- \"Trust has not commenced operations since incorporation. Commencement expected [date].\"\n- Attach the future activity plan\n\nThis is 100% acceptable. The IT Department grants Provisional Registration precisely for trusts in this stage \u2014 the whole point of \"provisional\" is to let trusts get tax status BEFORE they start operations, so they can operate compliantly from Day 1.\n\n**Do not worry about the 7-year gap** between trust deed (2019) and now (2026). It's not a legal problem for 12A/80G application \u2014 you just note that the trust was dormant.\n\n---\n\n## What You Can Do Right Now (Today/Sunday)\n\nSince you can't do anything on the CC side today, but want to be productive, here are things you CAN prepare in advance:\n\n### 1. Draft the \"Activities Note\"\n\nWrite a 1-2 page document titled **\"Trust Activities \u2014 Current Status and Future Plans\"**:\n- Brief history of trust (registered 2019, dormant, being activated 2026)\n- Current activities (none, or specifically list what you plan to start with)\n- Future activities planned for next 3 years (be specific \u2014 e.g., \"medical camps in Dwarka area,\" \"scholarship program for underprivileged students,\" \"old-age home support\")\n- Approximate budget estimates\n\nThis document will be uploaded with Form 10A. Having it ready now saves time.\n\n### 2. Prepare Trustees' Documents Bundle\n\nCreate a single PDF containing:\n- All 3 trustees' PAN cards (self-attested)\n- All 3 trustees' Aadhaar cards (self-attested)\n- Trust PAN card\n- Trust Deed\n\nThis is what you'll upload with Form 10A. Save time later.\n\n### 3. Decide on E-verification Method\n\nChoose one:\n- **Aadhaar OTP-based** \u2014 free, but requires Vishwa's Aadhaar-linked mobile to be active during filing\n- **Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)** \u2014 \u20b91,500-\u20b92,500 one-time cost, but easier for repeated filings\n\nFor a small trust just starting, Aadhaar OTP is fine. DSC becomes useful once operations scale.\n\n### 4. Plan the Bank Account Setup\n\nVerify with the bank:\n- Is the trust account a **current account or savings account**? (For trusts, current account is preferred)\n- Is **online banking activated** for the trust account? You'll need this for future compliance.\n- Is the **address on bank records** consistent with what we've entered on IT portal? Mismatch causes future headaches.\n\n### 5. Familiarize Yourself with Form 10A\n\nLog in (only for viewing, not filing) to the trust's IT portal account. Navigate:\n- **e-File** \u2192 **Income Tax Forms** \u2192 **File Income Tax Forms** \u2192 search for **Form 10A**\n\nJust view the form structure. Don't fill anything. Understanding the form fields in advance saves time when we file for real.\n\n---\n\n## To Answer Your Direct Question \u2014 Are You Eligible?\n\n**Yes, unequivocally.** Your trust meets all eligibility criteria for both **Provisional 12AB** and **Provisional 80G** registration.\n\nThe only pending piece is documentary proof of Charity Commissioner registration \u2014 which your lawyer will resolve when he visits Jamkhambhaliya after Monday. Once that document is in hand, we can file Form 10A within 24-48 hours.\n\nEverything else \u2014 trust structure, objectives, trustees, non-profit nature, universal benefit, non-political stance \u2014 is in perfect alignment with the requirements.\n\n---\n\nWant me to help you draft the **Activities Note** for Form 10A right now? That's the most valuable deliverable you can prepare while waiting for the CC status. If you tell me what activities you plan to start with (or want to start with) once operations begin, I can draft a solid 1-2 page document that will hold up perfectly for the 12A/80G application.",

                "uuid": "019f9b60-9386-715c-9aab-393903627132",
                "text": "Now coming to an important decision, as I got the authority to manage the trust, I called one of my fellow friend father who lives in USA from past 20 years and he's ready to give me donation. But can I take foreign donation?",
                "content": [
                    {
                        "start_timestamp": "2026-07-25T22:23:49.013511Z",
                        "stop_timestamp": "2026-07-25T22:23:49.013511Z",
                        "flags": null,
                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "Now coming to an important decision, as I got the authority to manage the trust, I called one of my fellow friend father who lives in USA from past 20 years and he's ready to give me donation. But can I take foreign donation?",
                        "citations": []
                    }
                ],
                "sender": "human",
                "created_at": "2026-07-25T22:23:49.013627Z",
                "updated_at": "2026-07-25T22:23:49.013627Z",

                "uuid": "019f9b60-9386-7f43-9662-6889761960cb",
                "text": "Stop. This is one of the most important decisions you'll face in the trust's early operations, and I need to be very direct with you.\n\n## Short Answer\n\n**No, you cannot legally accept a foreign donation right now. Not on Monday, not this month, not until the trust obtains FCRA registration.**\n\nAccepting foreign funds without FCRA registration is a **serious criminal offense** under Indian law. This isn't a technicality \u2014 this is genuinely one of the most heavily-enforced compliance areas in India, with recent history of thousands of NGOs having their licenses cancelled, funds frozen, and trustees prosecuted.\n\nLet me explain in detail so you understand exactly what's at stake.\n\n---\n\n## What is FCRA?\n\n**Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010** \u2014 a standalone law separate from Income Tax and Charity Commissioner regulations. It governs any receipt of \"foreign contribution\" by Indian NGOs, trusts, associations, or individuals for definite purposes.\n\n**Regulating authority:** Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Government of India \u2014 NOT the Income Tax Department or Charity Commissioner.\n\n**Why so strict?** After multiple national security concerns about foreign funding influencing Indian NGOs, the government has treated FCRA as a national security matter, not just a tax matter.\n\n---\n\n## What Counts as \"Foreign Contribution\"?\n\nUnder Section 2(1)(h) of FCRA, foreign contribution includes:\n\n1. **Any donation, delivery, or transfer** made by a **\"foreign source\"** of:\n - Currency (Indian or foreign)\n - Article (goods, gifts)\n - Securities\n\n2. **\"Foreign source\"** includes:\n - Foreign government\n - Foreign company\n - Foreign citizen\n - **NRI (Non-Resident Indian) \u2014 YES, this is critical**\n - Person of Indian Origin (PIO) with foreign citizenship\n - Any entity outside India\n\n### About Your Friend's Father\n\nYou said: *\"my fellow friend father who lives in USA from past 20 years.\"*\n\n**Critical question:** Is your friend's father:\n- **(a)** An **Indian citizen** who is currently residing in USA (holding Indian passport, NRI status)?\n- **(b)** A **US citizen** (naturalized, or born there \u2014 OCI/PIO card holder)?\n\n**These have DIFFERENT legal treatment:**\n\n### Scenario A: He is an Indian Citizen (NRI)\n**A donation from an NRI in foreign currency, or from a foreign bank account, IS foreign contribution and requires FCRA.**\n\nHowever, if he donates in **Indian Rupees from an Indian bank account** (e.g., his NRE/NRO account in India), the situation gets nuanced but is generally treated as domestic if the funds are from Indian sources.\n\n### Scenario B: He is a US Citizen (Even if of Indian Origin)\n**Any donation from him \u2014 in any currency, from any account, anywhere in the world \u2014 is 100% foreign contribution. Full stop.**\n\nThe moment he loses Indian citizenship, the government treats him as a \"foreign source\" regardless of ethnic/cultural background.\n\n**In most cases** \u2014 someone who has lived in USA for 20 years has likely either taken US citizenship (Scenario B) or holds long-term green card while maintaining Indian citizenship (Scenario A). You need to confirm which.\n\n---\n\n## Consequences of Accepting Foreign Contribution Without FCRA\n\nUnder **Section 35 of FCRA, 2010**:\n\n- **Imprisonment up to 5 years**, or fine, **or both**\n- **Confiscation of the foreign contribution received**\n- **Cancellation of any existing registrations** (12A, 80G would be jeopardized)\n- **Trustees held personally liable** \u2014 this is NOT limited to the trust\n\nUnder **Section 37**:\n- **Any officer/trustee** in charge at the time of contravention is deemed guilty\n\nUnder **Section 40**:\n- **Prohibition from receiving foreign contribution for 3 years** even after paying fines\n\n**And practically:**\n- Bank account frozen upon detection\n- Trust name on Ministry of Home Affairs blacklist\n- Future FCRA application virtually impossible\n- Any 12A/80G registration cancelled retrospectively\n- Reputation damage that cannot be undone\n\n**Recent enforcement:** In 2020-2024, over **20,000 NGOs had FCRA registrations cancelled** in India, including major, well-known charities. The government has actively investigated donations under \u20b91 lakh. This is not theoretical risk.\n\n---\n\n## What FCRA Registration Requires\n\nFCRA has strict eligibility criteria \u2014 and here's the difficult truth for you:\n\n### Minimum Prerequisites for FCRA Registration:\n\n1. **Trust must have existed for at least 3 years** \u26a0\ufe0f Your trust exists on paper for ~7 years but hasn't operated\n2. **Trust must have spent at least \u20b915 lakhs on charitable activities in the previous 3 years** \u274c You've spent zero\n3. **Must have proper accounts, audits, and returns for those 3 years** \u274c None\n4. **Must have 12A registration** \u274c Not yet obtained\n5. **Must have a dedicated FCRA bank account at SBI New Delhi Main Branch** \u2014 mandatory single-branch rule\n6. **Governing body members must not have criminal history**\n7. **Trust must not be involved in political activities**\n8. **NGO Darpan registration** \u2713 You have this\n\n**Realistic timeline for FCRA:** Your trust is **at least 3-4 years away** from being eligible for FCRA registration. This is by design \u2014 the government wants to see track record before allowing foreign funds.\n\n### Alternative \u2014 Prior Permission Route\n\nFCRA also allows **\"Prior Permission\"** for a specific foreign donation, even without full FCRA registration. But:\n- Application takes 3-6 months to process\n- Approval rate is low for new/unproven trusts\n- Requires all the same documents plus justification\n- Cannot be used for repeated donations\n\n---\n\n## What Are Your Actual Options Then?\n\nLet me lay out the realistic paths:\n\n### Option 1: Politely Decline (Recommended)\n\n**Explain to your friend's father** that:\n- You appreciate his generosity enormously\n- Indian law prohibits your trust from accepting foreign donations without FCRA registration\n- FCRA registration takes years and requires track record you don't have yet\n- Accepting his donation now would put the trust, trustees, and himself at legal risk\n- Once trust is established (3-4 years), you'll approach him again\n\nThis is the cleanest, most respectful, most legally safe option.\n\n### Option 2: Suggest He Donates in India Through Legal Means\n\n**If he has Indian bank accounts (NRE/NRO):** Even then, foreign contribution rules apply if he's not an Indian citizen. Consult a specialized FCRA lawyer before this route.\n\n**If he has family in India who can donate on his behalf:** His Indian-citizen relative can donate to your trust legally \u2014 but the money must be genuinely theirs, not routed from him. Any \"hawala-style\" routing would be illegal money laundering.\n\n### Option 3: Suggest He Donates to an Already-FCRA-Registered Trust with Similar Objectives\n\nIf his generosity is genuinely about your cause (charitable work in Dwarka), suggest an established FCRA-registered NGO doing similar work. Your objectives are broad (healthcare, education, water, etc.) \u2014 many established Gujarat-based NGOs would qualify.\n\n### Option 4: Wait Until FCRA Registration (Long-Term)\n\n- Build the trust's operations with domestic funds for 3 years\n- Establish track record with proper accounts\n- Then apply for FCRA\n- Then accept his donation legally\n\nThis is what your trust should aim for as a long-term goal.\n\n---\n\n## What You Should NOT Do\n\n- \u274c **Accept the donation \"quietly\" hoping no one notices** \u2014 banks report all foreign remittances to RBI/MHA automatically. Detection is virtually certain.\n\n- \u274c **Route it through someone else's account** \u2014 this is money laundering, a separate serious offense.\n\n- \u274c **Accept it as \"gift\" instead of donation** \u2014 FCRA covers gifts too.\n\n- \u274c **Accept it in his personal capacity and later \"convert\" to trust funds** \u2014 this creates a paper trail that becomes evidence.\n\n- \u274c **Convert USD to INR abroad and receive as cash in India** \u2014 this is hawala, criminally illegal.\n\n- \u274c **Take it and delay reporting** \u2014 non-disclosure aggravates the offense.\n\n---\n\n## A Broader Point About Trust Governance\n\nVraj, I want to say this directly and with care:\n\nYou've just been given the authority to manage this trust. In your first weeks, you're already navigating multiple complex compliance questions \u2014 CC registration status, 12A/80G, Vishwa as principal officer, address disputes on IT portal, and now foreign donations. That's a lot.\n\nThe reason for strict regulations like FCRA isn't to inconvenience honest trustees \u2014 it's because Indian charities have historically been misused for both intentional wrongdoing (money laundering, terror financing) and unintentional wrongdoing (well-meaning trustees not understanding rules). The government's position is: \"If you can't yet demonstrate that you'll be compliant, we won't yet trust you with sensitive channels like foreign money.\"\n\nYour trust is currently in the \"unproven\" phase. That's not an insult \u2014 it's just factual. **Your job in the first 2-3 years is to demonstrate that this trust operates cleanly, transparently, and effectively.** After that, doors open \u2014 80G scaling, CSR funding, FCRA, government grants, corporate partnerships.\n\nAccepting a foreign donation now \u2014 even from a well-meaning family friend \u2014 would close many of those doors permanently. It's not worth it.\n\n---\n\n## What to Say to Your Friend's Father\n\nIf you want a diplomatic message, here's a template:\n\n---\n\n*\"Uncleji, I'm deeply moved by your offer to support our trust. It means a lot to us that you'd be willing to contribute to work here in India.*\n\n*Unfortunately, Indian law has strict rules about foreign contributions to charitable trusts \u2014 even from Indian-origin individuals living abroad. Our trust needs a specific registration called FCRA before we can legally accept any foreign donation, and this registration requires 3 years of proven charitable operations, which we're just now beginning.*\n\n*I hope you understand that accepting your donation now, even with pure intent on both sides, would put the trust, our trustees, and even yourself at legal risk. I'd rather build the trust properly over the next few years, obtain the necessary FCRA registration, and then gratefully receive your support \u2014 knowing everything is fully in order.*\n\n*In the meantime, if you have family here in India who share the vision, they could contribute on their own behalf. Or, if you'd like your generosity to reach India sooner, I can suggest some established FCRA-registered NGOs doing similar charitable work.*\n\n*Thank you for your understanding and continued blessings. We'll stay in touch as the trust grows.\"*\n\n---\n\n## The One Question You Need to Confirm\n\nBefore we close this topic entirely \u2014 please confirm:\n\n**Is your friend's father an Indian citizen (with US green card / long-term visa) or a US citizen (naturalized)?**\n\nIf he's still an Indian citizen residing in USA, there are some narrow scenarios where he could donate through his Indian-domiciled income (e.g., rental income from Indian property, deposited in his NRO account, then donated in INR). This is still nuanced and I'd want you to consult an FCRA lawyer before pursuing \u2014 but it's technically possible.\n\nIf he's a US citizen, then it's a clean no until FCRA is obtained.\n\nPlease confirm his citizenship status, and I'll advise more precisely.",
